name: Utah

statute.name: Government Records Access and Management Act (GRAMA)

response.rule_text: Entity must respond to a written request no later than ten business days after receipt (five for qualifying expedited requests); missing the deadline is treated as a denial that can be appealed (Utah Code ch. 63G-2, per RCFP).

fees.labor_rule: Staff search/retrieval time chargeable only when the record must be compiled in a form not normally maintained (§ 63G-2-203(2)); no fee for review or inspection (§ 63G-2-203(5)(b)).
fees.waiver_rule: Waivers encouraged when release primarily benefits the public; news media presumed to qualify (§ 63G-2-203(4)(a)).
fees.estimate_required: Entity may require payment of estimated fees if over $50 or past fees unpaid; excess refunded (§ 63G-2-203(8)).
fees.late_penalty: Attorney fees if requester substantially prevails on judicial appeal (§ 63G-2-802(3)(a)).

residency.rule_text: Not addressed in the fetched RCFP text; the right to inspect is stated for 'a person' (§ 63G-2-201(1)).

appeal.body: Chief administrative officer, then Government Records Office director (§ 63A-12-203), then district court
appeal.rule_text: Appeal to the entity's chief administrative officer, who decides in five business days; then to the Government Records Office director within 30 days of the final determination (45 days after the request if none), who decides within 73 days; district court generally within 30 days of the order. Ombudsman mediates (§ 63A-12-204).

format_rule: Entity need not provide a record in a format, medium, or program not currently maintained (§ 63G-2-201(7)(a)(iii)); storage form may not be used to hinder access (§ 63G-2-201(12)).
notes: Read chars 0-100k and 150-250k. Extension for extraordinary circumstances (e.g. 5 more business days for legal issues, 15 for extensive editing). 30-day unit assumed calendar. Legislature covered but not subject to GRAMA fee/appeal provisions (§ 63G-2-703(2)(a)). RCFP does not mention State Records Committee.
